title: LeadTriageOutput

evidence.description: Every item must be traceable to a field in the input record. This is the visible 'scoring matrix' rationale — what specifically drove this score.

draft_message.description: The automatic first-contact acknowledgment. Required (non-null) whenever needs_human_input is false — every scored lead gets an instant acknowledgment, not just high-scoring ones.

x_worker_side_validation_rules: If needs_human_input == true, draft_message MUST be null.
If needs_human_input == false, draft_message MUST be present (every scored lead gets an acknowledgment).
recommended_action.playbook_code MUST match lead_score's fixed mapping in lead_playbook.json — this is a hard, blocking gate.
draft_message.channel MUST be a method this lead actually has available (contact_phone_available/contact_email_available) — this is a hard, blocking gate.

Every string in scoring.evidence is spot-checked against the input record's observed/inferred fields as a NON-BLOCKING transparency note only (as of this revision) — after repeated real false positives from an LLM's phrasing variability, an unverifiable citation is logged but does not by itself set review_flag = true.

auto_send is granted (computed by the Worker, not the model) only when review_flag == false AND needs_human_input == false AND draft_message is present — this is the one gate between 'automatic' and 'held for human review'.  Only the playbook-mismatch and channel-availability rules above can set review_flag = true on their own.
